In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IPF and EEA are characterized by a complex and dynamic interplay between pro- and anti-angiogenic mediators that may differ in the various stages of disease.
the role of the chemokine system in IPF and in EAA is complex and multifaceted.
IPF and EAE share many similarities, but the underlying pathogenesis is different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IPF is an angiostatic disease and that EAA is an angiogenic disease, and that the two are distinct.
we have identified the first angiostatic chemokine, CXCL10, in the lungs of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and emphysema.
the angiogenic chemokine, CCL2, is upregulated in both EAA and IPF and is a key mediator of fibroblast activation and fibrosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemokines CCL2 and CCL5, which are known for their angiogenic activity in the context of tumorigenesis, also have angiostatic properties in the context of fibrotic disease.
we have shown that a single intravenous injection of a small molecule, which we have called a "chemical chaperone," can reverse the pathology of IPF in a mouse model of IPF.
the angiogenic chemokine CXCL8 is a key player in IPF, whereas the angiostatic CXCL10 is a key player of EAA.
